category: X10-F3 Map, context and scene-prior consistency
title: Fusion of map matching and traffic sign recognition

Cost not read.
notes: Crossref search record only (no abstract). Not an attack paper; kept as the map-prior building block named in the brief leads.

category: X10-F1 Camera-LiDAR and multi-sensor consistency defenses
title: Invisible for both Camera and LiDAR: Security of Multi-Sensor Fusion based Perception in Autonomous Driving Under Physical-World Attacks
venue: 2021 IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy (SP)
key_idea: Tests the core fusion assumption that not every sensor is attacked at once: one optimised, 3D-printed object fools camera and LiDAR together, so fused perception misses it and the vehicle can hit it.
method: Optimisation of a physical object against both sensing pipelines, with workarounds for non-differentiable camera and LiDAR sensing and for cell-level aggregated LiDAR features; tested on open-source industry-grade fusion.
data: Fusion modules of open-source industry-grade AD systems in real-world driving scenarios; 3D-printed objects captured by LiDAR and camera devices; simulation for end-to-end safety impact (abstract).
reported_result: Abstract: over 90% attack success across object types and fusion algorithms; stealthy, robust to victim position, transferable across fusion algorithms and physically realisable.
relation_to_project: Notes question 1 against sensor fusion: camera-LiDAR redundancy is no guarantee, because one physical object can attack both sources. Fusion does not make a camera-side cue check redundant; such a check would face the same coordinated-object threat (inference).
notes: Crossref record (IEEE S&P 2021) and arXiv record 2106.09249 both read; abstract from the arXiv record, cut at the end. The authors novelty wording is not repeated. A 2022 AutoSec demo of the same work is in the ledger (DOI 10.14722/autosec.2022.23038), not catalogued.

category: X10-F1 Camera-LiDAR and multi-sensor consistency defenses
title: Adversarial Robustness of Deep Sensor Fusion Models
venue: 2022 IEEE/CVF Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision (WACV)
key_idea: Experimental study of camera-LiDAR fusion for 2D detection: fusion is usually more accurate and more robust to single-source attacks than one sensor, but adversarial training on one channel can hurt robustness on the other.
method: Single-source and joint attacks on early and late fusion detectors, with and without single-channel, box-restricted and joint-channel adversarial training.
data: Camera-LiDAR fusion architectures for 2D object detection in driving (abstract; dataset not named).
reported_result: Abstract: early fusion more robust than late fusion without adversarial training and similar after it; cross-channel externalities; joint-channel training mitigates several issues but does not raise robustness significantly. No numbers in the abstract.
relation_to_project: Notes question 1: fusion helps against digital single-source attacks, yet hardening it is costly and brittle (training, two sensors). Supports testing a cheap runtime cue check beside fusion; digital perturbations, not physical.
notes: Crossref record (WACV 2022) and arXiv record 2006.13192 (2020) both read; abstract from the arXiv record.

category: X10-F1 Camera-LiDAR and multi-sensor consistency defenses
title: Defending Multimodal Fusion Models against Single-Source Adversaries
venue: 2021 IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR)
key_idea: Shows an attack on any single modality can override correct information from the others, then trains a fusion layer that compares the sources, detects the inconsistent one and passes only information from unperturbed sources.
method: Adversarially robust fusion strategy trained to spot cross-modal inconsistency and gate out the perturbed modality; evaluated on several multimodal tasks.
data: Multimodal action recognition, object detection and sentiment analysis tasks (abstract; datasets not named).
reported_result: Abstract: single-source robustness gains of 19.7 to 48.2% on object detection (7.8 to 25.2% action recognition, 1.6 to 6.7% sentiment analysis) without loss on clean data.
relation_to_project: Closest cross-sensor analogue of the slide pipeline: an explicit inconsistency test between independent sources that decides which source to trust. Needs a second modality and a retrained fusion model, unlike a frozen detector plus a cheap camera cue; digital worst-case perturbations, not physical attacks.
notes: Crossref record (CVPR 2021) and arXiv record 2206.12714 (posted 2022) both read; abstract from the arXiv record. Which sensors the object detection task fuses is not stated in the abstract.

category: X10-F1 Camera-LiDAR and multi-sensor consistency defenses
title: Exploring Adversarial Robustness of Multi-Sensor Perception Systems in Self Driving
key_idea: One universal adversarial object placed on a car roof hides different host vehicles from LiDAR-image fusion detectors; the attacks succeed mainly through easily corrupted image features.
method: Physically realisable, input-agnostic adversarial object consistent across LiDAR and camera; adversarial training with feature denoising evaluated as defense.
data: State-of-the-art multi-modal LiDAR-image detectors (abstract; dataset not named).
reported_result: Abstract: one universal adversary hides different vehicles; fusion that projects image features into 3D can be exploited to create distant false positives; adversarial training with feature denoising helps markedly, but false positives from wrong LiDAR-pixel association remain.
relation_to_project: Inside fusion the camera branch is the weak link, so camera-side evidence checks stay needed even with LiDAR (notes question 3). Fabricated distant boxes are a target for a geometry or context plausibility cue (hypothesis).
notes: Preprint record, verified against the arXiv API only (2021). A conference version is recalled from memory, venue UNVERIFIED: check the published version before citing.

category: X10-F1 Camera-LiDAR and multi-sensor consistency defenses
title: Fusion is Not Enough: Single Modal Attacks on Fusion Models for 3D Object Detection
key_idea: Camera-only deployable patches defeat camera-LiDAR fusion 3D detectors: the most vulnerable modality sets the robustness of the fused model, against the view of fusion as a general defense.
method: Two-stage optimisation: locate the image areas most sensitive to attack, then apply fusion-model-specific strategies to produce deployable patches.
data: Six camera-LiDAR fusion 3D detectors and one camera-only detector (abstract; dataset not named).
reported_result: Abstract: all seven models compromised; detection mAP falls from 0.824 to 0.353, or the detection score of a target object from 0.728 to 0.156.
relation_to_project: Strong support for the problem statement: adding LiDAR does not remove the camera patch threat, so a camera-side check is still needed. Its patches are a natural attack set for testing slide 01 behind a fusion detector.
notes: Preprint record, verified against the arXiv API only (2023). The abstract says code is available; location not seen. A conference version is recalled from memory, venue UNVERIFIED.

category: X10-F1 Camera-LiDAR and multi-sensor consistency defenses
title: Security Analysis of Camera-LiDAR Fusion Against Black-Box Attacks on Autonomous Vehicles
key_idea: Plain LiDAR spoofing does not disrupt camera-LiDAR fusion, but a context-aware frustum attack that keeps camera and LiDAR semantics consistent fools all tested detectors and evades existing spoofing defenses.
method: Black-box LiDAR spoofing placed consistently with the camera view of a real object (frustum attack); tested on LiDAR-only and fusion detectors and over time against tracking and control.
data: 8 perception algorithms across 3 LiDAR-only and 3 camera-LiDAR fusion architectures (abstract).
reported_result: Abstract: all 8 algorithms significantly vulnerable; the attack stays stealthy to existing LiDAR spoofing defenses because cross-sensor semantic consistency is preserved; sustained attack sequences compromise tracking and end-to-end control.
relation_to_project: Threat to every consistency check: an attacker who knows the check keeps the checked relation true (the same lesson as ADC, P2-P516, for scene context). A slide 01 to 05 residual needs an adaptive test where the attacker preserves the cue.
notes: Preprint record, verified against the arXiv API only (2021). A security-conference version is recalled from memory, venue UNVERIFIED. LiDAR-side attack: kept as evidence on cross-sensor consistency, not as a camera attack.

category: X10-F1 Camera-LiDAR and multi-sensor consistency defenses
title: Monitoring and Diagnosability of Perception Systems
venue: 2021 IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS)
key_idea: Graph-theoretic runtime monitor that detects faults in a perception system from consistency tests between modules with different outputs over time, and bounds how many faulty modules can be detected.
method: Diagnosability theory for multiprocessor systems generalised to heterogeneous module outputs and a temporal dimension; diagnostic graph of consistency tests; topos-theory formulation.
reported_result: Abstract: runtime fault detection and an upper bound on the number of detectable faulty modules; no numbers in the abstract.
relation_to_project: Formal frame for notes question 3: consistency tests can locate a fault only with enough redundant modules. With a frozen detector and one cue, a disagreement shows that one of them is wrong but not which (inference from the theory), which is why the slides need the benign or abstain branch.
notes: Crossref record (IROS 2021) and arXiv record 2005.11816 (2020) both read; abstract from the arXiv record. Not attack-specific: faults of any cause. Also in the LIT_X13 ledger; coordinator to deduplicate if LIT_X13 adds a row.

title: On Data Fabrication in Collaborative Vehicular Perception: Attacks and Countermeasures
key_idea: Malicious participants in collaborative perception send crafted data that cause hard brakes or collision risk; benign vehicles jointly reveal the fabrication with an anomaly detector built on agreement across their views.
method: Real-time data fabrication attacks on shared perception data; systematic anomaly detection in which benign vehicles cross-check the shared perception jointly.
data: High-fidelity simulated scenarios and real-world experiments (abstract).
reported_result: Abstract: attack success over 86% in simulation; the countermeasure detects 91.5% of attacks at a 3% false-positive rate in simulation and reduces attack impact in real-world runs.
relation_to_project: Multi-view consistency reported at a fixed false-positive rate, the reporting style the slides require. Needs other vehicles and V2X; the threat is a malicious data sender, not a physical object seen by one camera.
notes: Preprint record, verified against the arXiv API only (2023). Attack and countermeasure in one paper; role DETECTION chosen for this family. A security-conference version is recalled from memory, venue UNVERIFIED.

title: Among Us: Adversarially Robust Collaborative Perception by Consensus
venue: 2023 IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision (ICCV)
key_idea: ROBOSAC: collaboration should agree with individual perception, so results with and without random subsets of teammates are compared until consensus, rejecting attackers without knowing the attack.
method: Hypothesize-and-verify sampling over teammate subsets; analysis of how many trials guarantee an attacker-free subset of a given size, or the largest such subset within a trial budget.
data: Collaborative 3D object detection in autonomous driving scenarios (abstract; dataset not named).
reported_result: Abstract: validated on collaborative 3D detection; no numbers in the abstract.
relation_to_project: Attack-agnostic consensus check with an explicit trade-off between sampling time and assurance, a model for bounding the compute of a consistency test. Needs several agents; not usable by one camera.
notes: Crossref record (ICCV 2023) and arXiv record 2303.09495 both read; abstract from the arXiv record.

title: MADE: Malicious Agent Detection for Robust Multi-Agent Collaborative Perception
venue: 2024 IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS)
key_idea: Each agent tests every collaborator for consistency with its own view through two hypothesis tests and removes agents judged malicious, with the false-positive rate controlled by the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure.
method: Semi-supervised anomaly detector; double hypothesis test on a match-loss statistic and a collaborative reconstruction-loss statistic, both measuring ego-collaborator consistency.
reported_result: Abstract: average-precision drop against an oracle defender of 1.28% (V2X-Sim) and 0.34% (DAIR-V2X), against 8.92% and 10.00% for adversarial training.
relation_to_project: A consistency statistic turned into a calibrated test with explicit false-positive control: a template for the matched false-alarm operating point and the abstain logic of slides 01 to 05. Needs collaborators; feature-level attacks, not physical.
notes: Crossref record (IROS 2024) carries the MADE prefix; arXiv record 2310.11901 (2023) has the title without it. Abstract from the arXiv record.

title: CP-Guard+: A New Paradigm for Malicious Agent Detection and Defense in Multi-Agent Collaborative Perception
venue: IEEE Transactions on Dependable and Secure Computing
key_idea: Title only: detection of and defense against malicious agents in multi-agent collaborative perception, presented by the authors as a new paradigm.
relation_to_project: Most recent record found in the collaborative-consistency line (after ROBOSAC and MADE); shows the line is active in 2026 and still needs other agents, not one camera.
notes: Crossref search record only; the arXiv search for it was cut by the arXiv stop. NEEDS_VERIFY: abstract. A related TDSC 2026 paper, GCP (spatial-temporal aware malicious agent detection), was seen only as a supplementary-file record; lead not confirmed.

title: Understanding the Robustness of 3D Object Detection with Bird's-Eye-View Representations in Autonomous Driving
key_idea: Benchmarks natural and adversarial robustness of multi-camera BEV 3D detectors and adds a patch attack placed in 3D space so that it stays consistent across views and time.
method: Evaluation of BEV and non-BEV camera detectors and of BEV fusion under corruptions and adversarial noise; 3D-consistent patch attack.
data: Representative camera BEV detectors and camera-LiDAR BEV fusion detectors (abstract; dataset not named).
reported_result: Abstract: BEV models more stable under natural corruptions but more vulnerable to adversarial noise; BEV fusion still vulnerable to point-cloud and image noise. No numbers in the abstract.
relation_to_project: Notes question 3 for multi-view: an attack made consistent across cameras and frames defeats checks that rely on view or time disagreement. Defines the attack class a viewpoint-aware check (slide 01) must face.
notes: Preprint record, verified against the arXiv API only (2023). A conference version is recalled from memory, venue UNVERIFIED.

title: On the Adversarial Robustness of Camera-based 3D Object Detection
key_idea: Studies leading camera-based 3D detectors under white-box and black-box, pixel and patch attacks on classification and localisation; finds that benign multi-frame input and accurate depth both improve robustness.
method: Systematic attack evaluation across detector families (BEV, depth-estimation-based, depth-free), two attack settings, two objectives and two attack types.
data: Camera-based 3D object detectors (abstract; dataset not named).
reported_result: Abstract findings: BEV representations resist localisation attacks better; depth-free methods may be more robust; accurate depth helps depth-based methods; benign multi-frame inputs mitigate attacks. No numbers in the abstract.
relation_to_project: Evidence that clean evidence from other frames dilutes an attack, which supports the temporal and multi-view consistency idea behind slides 01 and 05; digital attacks on 3D detectors, not physical sign attacks.
notes: Preprint record, verified against the arXiv API only (2023). A journal version is recalled from memory, venue UNVERIFIED. The authors novelty wording is not repeated.
